initial_observation.demographics: Patient of 25 years old, primigravida primiparous
initial_observation.encounter_context: referred to us at D1 (day 1 postpartum) for acute pubic pain after delivery in a peripheral hospital
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: The pregnancy was not followed and was without incidents; delivery occurred at term in a peripheral hospital with a male newborn weighing 4400 g; patient referred at Day 1 postpartum for acute pubic pain
presenting_symptoms: increased abdomino-pelvic sensitivity to palpation of the pubic symphysis
known_prior_history: no notion of pelvic pain during pregnancy

evidence_items.source_text: The clinical examination showed an increased abdomino-pelvic sensitivity to palpation of the pubic symphysis.
An X-ray of the pelvis showed a pubic disjunction

the abdomino-pelvic CT confirmed the diagnosis of a 3 cm pubic symphysis disjunction with no detectable fracture and infiltration of the soft tissues in front of the symphysis without any detectable collection. The sacroiliac and coxo-femoral joints were normal (Fig. 1, Fig. 2)
the therapeutic management consisted of unloading and preventive anti-coagulation, with analgesic treatment based on paracetamol and NSAID.
The evolution was favorable without painful recurrence. The examination at the time of the control carried out after 15 days does not objective sensitivity at the symphysial level.
An X-ray of the pelvis showed a pubic disjunction, the abdomino-pelvic CT confirmed the diagnosis of a 3 cm pubic symphysis disjunction

hidden_reference.final_diagnosis_verbatim: pubic symphysis disjunction syndrome following a dystocic delivery
